gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 12 build gate now carries a dedicated virtio_scsi survey so this complex-driver lane stays reviewable without pretending a drivers/scsi starter already exists.
The existing make target keeps the survey lane runnable in the same bounded way as the other tranche checkpoints instead of hiding it behind ad hoc commands.

The Phase 10 virtio core slice already covers status sequencing, feature negotiation, queue callback bookkeeping, descriptor-shape metadata, and notification accounting, which is the minimum shared footing a future virtio_scsi probe snapshot would depend on.

The existing virtio_ring helper keeps queue-shape and notification bookkeeping in memory only, which is the closest current Zigux surface for describing virtio_scsi control, event, and request virtqueue topology without claiming DMA-backed queue execution.
A dedicated survey test is the smallest truthful way to record that virtio_scsi.c is present, Phase 10 virtio groundwork exists, and the repo still has no drivers/scsi/virtio_scsi.zig starter.
The lane needs a note that spells out the real scope of virtio_scsi.c so future runs do not confuse a large production SCSI HBA with a ready-to-port helper slice.

The next honest virtio_scsi step is one tiny probe-time snapshot helper around num_queues, seg_max, cmd_per_lun, max_target, max_lun, max_sectors, and control or event versus request virtqueue topology so the lane can describe virtscsi_probe() before any blk-mq, DMA, or SCSI host registration work.

Command submission, TMF and async notification handling, event-work scheduling, freeze or restore flows, virtqueue buffer ownership, scsi_add_host(), scsi_scan_host(), and live blk-mq or DMA-backed request handling remain blocked until a much smaller probe snapshot exists and the roadmap-approved queueing and transport substrate is in place.
